name: Bundles, Safety & Ethics
sub: SSC bundle, ABCDEF, VAP/CLABSI/CAUTI, delirium, end of life, scoring

cards.q: List the Hour-1 sepsis bundle elements.
cards.a: Measure lactate (re-measure if >2 mmol/L), obtain blood cultures before antibiotics, give broad-spectrum antibiotics, give at least 30 mL/kg crystalloid for hypotension or lactate ≥4 (still suggested in SSC 2026, but individualise and reassess), and start vasopressors to keep MAP ≥65 mmHg.

cards.q: How soon should antibiotics be given in septic shock?
cards.a: Immediately, ideally within 1 hour, for septic shock or probable/definite sepsis; within 3 hours for possible sepsis without shock after rapid assessment.

cards.q: What does the ABCDEF bundle include?
cards.a: Assess and manage pain, Both spontaneous awakening and breathing trials, Choice of analgesia and sedation, Delirium assessment and management, Early mobility, Family engagement.

cards.q: What is the ventilator-associated pneumonia prevention bundle?
cards.a: Head-of-bed elevation 30–45°, daily sedation interruption and readiness to extubate, oral care (chlorhexidine is debated), subglottic secretion drainage, and avoiding unnecessary ventilation or circuit changes.

cards.q: What is the CLABSI prevention bundle?
cards.a: Hand hygiene, maximal barrier precautions, chlorhexidine skin antisepsis, optimal site selection (avoid femoral), daily review of necessity, and prompt removal.

cards.q: What are the CAUTI prevention steps?
cards.a: Insert only for appropriate indications, aseptic insertion, closed drainage, daily review and early removal, avoid routine irrigation.

cards.q: Define SOFA score components and how it is used.
cards.a: Respiration (PaO₂/FiO₂), coagulation (platelets), liver (bilirubin), cardiovascular (MAP/vasopressors), CNS (GCS), renal (creatinine/urine output). A rise of ≥2 points defines organ dysfunction in sepsis.

cards.q: What is qSOFA?
cards.a: Respiratory rate ≥22/min, altered mentation, systolic BP ≤100 mmHg; ≥2 predicts poor outcome. SSC 2026 suggests NEWS/NEWS2, MEWS or SIRS rather than qSOFA alone for screening.

cards.q: How do you define APACHE II and its use?
cards.a: Acute Physiology and Chronic Health Evaluation: 12 physiological variables, age and chronic health points to predict hospital mortality and benchmark ICU care.

cards.q: What is the Richmond Agitation–Sedation Scale (RASS) target?
cards.a: Light sedation: RASS 0 to −2 in most ventilated patients.

cards.q: What is the CPOT/BPS scale used for?
cards.a: Pain assessment in non-communicating ICU patients (Critical-Care Pain Observation Tool, Behavioural Pain Scale).

cards.q: List the criteria for a spontaneous breathing trial pass.
cards.a: RR <35/min, SpO₂ ≥90% on FiO₂ ≤0.4–0.5, HR <140 without significant change, no distress or sweating, rapid shallow breathing index <105 over 30–120 minutes.

cards.q: What is the structure of a family meeting in the ICU?
cards.a: VALUE: Value statements, Acknowledge emotions, Listen, Understand the patient as a person, Elicit questions (and use REMAP or similar frameworks for goals-of-care).

cards.q: What distinguishes withholding from withdrawing life-sustaining treatment?
cards.a: Both are ethically equivalent when treatment is non-beneficial or declined; apply a documented process, palliative care, symptom control and family support.

cards.q: What is the legal position on passive euthanasia in India?
cards.a: The Supreme Court (Common Cause v Union of India, 2018, with 2023 modifications) recognises advance directives and withdrawal of life-sustaining treatment under defined procedures with medical boards.

cards.q: Outline the steps of a root-cause analysis after a patient-safety incident.
cards.a: Report promptly, secure the patient and evidence, assemble a multidisciplinary team, map the timeline, identify contributing factors, agree actions with owners and review effectiveness.

cards.q: What is the Surviving Sepsis recommendation for fluid choice?
cards.a: Crystalloids first-line (strong); balanced crystalloids suggested over saline (saline preferred in TBI); albumin may suit large volumes or cirrhosis; recommend against starches and suggest against gelatins.

cards.q: What is the transfusion-of-donor-organs checklist before ICU brain-death donation?
cards.a: Optimise haemodynamics (MAP ≥65), oxygenation, normothermia, sodium 135–145, glucose control, hormone replacement as required, and communicate early with the organ procurement team.

cards.q: Which of these is part of the ABCDEF bundle?
o: Both spontaneous awakening and breathing trials
Prophylactic antibiotics for all ventilated patients
cards.e: The ABCDEF bundle couples SAT/SBT coordination with analgesia first, delirium management and early mobility.

cards.q: A patient presents with suspected septic shock. What should happen before giving antibiotics, if it does not delay them?
o: Perform lumbar puncture in all cases
cards.e: Take blood cultures as soon as possible and ideally before antibiotics, without delaying them (SSC 2026, strong; the 2021 text used about 45 minutes).
